title: Papa Tora’ah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Mentioned in [Gittin 19a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.19a.16), where Rav Papa gave him a ruling. Hyman quotes [Rashi’s explanation](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Gittin.19a.16.2) of the epithet as “an ox broker.”[^1][^2]

notes.text: The supplied Hebrew gloss is סופר של שוורים, “scribe of oxen.” The linked Rashi instead reads ספסר של שוורים, “ox broker.”

Hyman’s printed entry (vol. III, p. 1029) reads סרסר, “broker,” where the supplied Hebrew reads סופר, “scribe.” The consulted Rashi at Gittin 19a reads ספסר, also “broker,” while the Davidson translation of the Talmud calls Pappa an ox herder. The Talmud distinguishes Rav Pappa, who gave the ruling, from Papa Tora’ah, who received it.
